questions.q: What does `dbt build` do that running `dbt run` and `dbt test` separately does not?
options: Runs every model and every test together, in dependency order, in one command
Only runs tests, skipping all models
Deletes and recreates the entire Snowflake database
Only works on staging models, never on marts
questions.explain: dbt build interleaves models and tests in dependency order in a single pass, rather than requiring two separate commands.

questions.q: In this project's real dbt build output, why does the mart model (customers) run last?
options: The dependency graph builds staging first, runs its tests, and only then builds the mart that depends on it
Model order is alphabetical, and 'customers' comes after 'stg_jaffle_shop'
dbt always runs mart models before staging models
The order is random each time dbt build runs
questions.explain: The order in a dbt build run reflects the dependency graph, not file order — staging must succeed (including its tests) before the mart that ref()s it is built.

questions.q: What line should you check first in any dbt build output, according to this lesson?
options: Done. PASS=... WARN=... ERROR=... SKIP=... TOTAL=...
Found N models, N data tests
Concurrency: N threads
The first START line
questions.explain: The final summary line — Done. PASS=... ERROR=... — is the one line to check first, always, since it tells you at a glance whether everything succeeded.

questions.q: If the unique test on customer_id had failed during this dbt build run, what would happen to the customers mart model?
options: It would be SKIPped, since dbt won't build a model on top of data already known to be broken
It would still build normally, since tests and models are independent
dbt would automatically delete the duplicate row and continue
The entire Snowflake database would be dropped
questions.explain: dbt's dependency graph protects downstream models: if a test on an upstream model fails, anything depending on that model gets SKIPped rather than built on bad data.

questions.q: How does the Done. PASS=4 ERROR=0 output connect back to Lesson 1's original ask?
options: It's the literal, checkable proof that the customer list is trustworthy — not a claim, but a passing automated check anyone can rerun
It has no connection; Lesson 1 was only about requirements, not technical outcomes
It proves the Ops Manager personally approved the table
PASS=4 means exactly 4 customers exist in the table
questions.explain: Lesson 1 asked for a trustworthy customer list; the dbt build summary line is the concrete, rerunnable evidence that the project delivered exactly that.
